   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Basis of presentation and summary of significant accounting policies </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">The accompanying unaudited&#160;interim consolidated financial statements reflect the accounts of the Company for the quarterly period ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>&#160;(the &#8220;Financial Statements&#8221;). The Financial Statements were prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial information and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) for interim financial information. Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and notes required by U.S. GAAP and should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements (the &#8220;Annual Financial Statements&#8221;) included in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>&#160;(the &#8220;Annual Report&#8221;). These&#160;Financial Statements reflect all adjustments, which, in the opinion of management, are necessary for a fair presentation of the results for the interim periods presented. Interim results are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results for the&#160;full fiscal year.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The&#160;Financial Statements have been prepared on a&#160;going concern basis, which assumes that the Company will continue in operation for the foreseeable future and, accordingly, will be able to realize its assets and discharge its liabilities in the normal course of operations as they come due, under the historical cost convention except for certain financial instruments that are measured at fair value, as detailed in the Company&#8217;s accounting policies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">All amounts in the Financial Statements, and the accompanying notes and tables have been rounded to the nearest thousand, except par values and per share amounts, and unless otherwise indicated.</p>

Control exists when the Company either has a controlling voting interest or is the primary beneficiary of a variable interest entity. The financial statements of all subsidiaries are included in the Financial Statements from the date that control commences until the date that control ceases. All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated on consolidation. A complete list of our subsidiaries that existed as of our most recent fiscal year end is included in the Annual Report.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28" name="tlry:DigitalAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142767956" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Digital Assets</i></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08,</em>&#160;Intangibles&#8212;Goodwill and Other&#8212;Crypto Assets (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">350</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">60</em>): Accounting for and Disclosure of Crypto Assets. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> requires certain crypto assets to be measured at fair value separately on the balance sheet with gains and losses from changes in the fair value reported as unrealized gains or losses in the consolidated statement of&#160;income (loss) and comprehensive income (loss) each reporting period. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> also enhances the other intangible asset disclosure requirements by requiring the name, cost basis, fair value, and number of units for each significant crypto asset holding.&#160;In conjunction with the acquisition of digital assets during the fiscal quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> August 31, 2025, </em>the Company adopted and applied ASU-<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> henceforth.&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">The Company's digital assets are initially recorded at cost, and are subsequently measured at fair value as of each reporting period. The Company determines the fair value of its digital assets in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em>&#160;Fair Value Measurement, based on quoted prices in&#160;its principal market for Bitcoin (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>). Changes in fair value are recognized as incurred in the Company's consolidated statement of income (loss) and comprehensive income (loss), as &#8220;Unrealized (gain) loss on digital assets,&#8221; within&#160;non-operating (income) and expenses, net.&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142767957" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>New accounting pronouncements</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">not</em></i>&#160;<i>yet adopted</i></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 2023,&#160;</em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em>&#160;Business Combination - Joint Venture Formations&#160;(Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">805</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">60</em>) Recognition and Initial Measurement (&#8220;ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05&#8221;</em>), which is intended to address the accounting for contributions made to a joint venture. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2026.&#160;</em>This update will be applied prospectively and the Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> October&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em>&#160;the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em>&#160;Disclosure Improvements: Codification Amendments in Response to the SEC&#8217;s Disclosure Update and Simplification Initiative,&#160;which amends the disclosure or presentation requirements related to various subtopics in the FASB Accounting Standards Codification (the &#8220;Codification&#8221;). The effective date for each amendment will be the date on which the SEC&#8217;s removal of that related disclosure from Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em>&#160;or Regulation S-K becomes effective, with early adoption prohibited. If by <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2027,&#160;</em>the SEC has&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;removed the applicable requirement from Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em>&#160;or Regulation S-K, the pending content of the related amendment will be removed from the Codification and will&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;become effective for any entity.&#160;The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em>&#160;Income Taxes (Topic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">740</em>)&#160;Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures,&#160;which requires public entities to disclose specific categories in the rate reconciliation and provide additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative threshold on an annual basis. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning with its&#160;fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2026&#160;</em>and will be disclosed&#160;in the Financial&#160;Statements reported in our Annual Report on Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K filed with the SEC for such period.&#160;The Company is in the process of evaluating the impact of the financial statement disclosure requirement.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses,&#160;which requires disaggregated disclosure of income statement expenses for public business entities. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2028&#160;</em>and will be disclosed&#160;in the Annual Report on Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for such period.&#160;The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>New accounting pronouncements recently adopted</i></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04,</em>&#160;Debt with Conversion and Other Options (Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">470</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em>): Induced Conversions of Convertible Debt Instruments,&#160;which seeks to clarify the requirements for determining whether certain settlements of convertible debt instruments should be accounted for as an induced conversion. The Company adopted ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04</em>&#160;beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025,&#160;</em>however, it&#160;did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have any impact on our unaudited&#160;interim consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

Changes in the carrying amount are&#160;recorded in the consolidated statement of net loss and comprehensive loss. During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, the Company also completed the sale of the Fort Collins asset group. The loss on the disposition of assets held for sale are&#160;recorded in the consolidated statement of loss.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;convertible debentures&#160;were issued&#160;on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2023 </em>and on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 9, 2023 </em>by way of overallotment,&#160;in the principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764339" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">172,500</ix:nonFraction> (the &#8220;TLRY <em style="font: inherit;">27</em> Notes&#8221;). The TLRY <em style="font: inherit;">27</em> Notes&#160;bear interest at a rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142764342" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.20</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15&#160;</em>of each year, and mature on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2027,&#160;</em>unless earlier converted. The TLRY <em style="font: inherit;">27</em> Notes are Tilray&#8217;s general unsecured obligations and rank senior in right of payment to all of Tilray&#8217;s indebtedness that is expressly subordinated in right of payment to the notes; equal in right of payment with any of Tilray&#8217;s unsecured indebtedness that is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> so subordinated,&#160;effectively junior in right of payment to any of Tilray&#8217;s secured indebtedness to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness; and structurally junior to all indebtedness and other liabilities (including trade payables but excluding intercompany obligations) of Tilray&#8217;s current or future subsidiaries.&#160;Noteholders have the right to convert their TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes into shares of Tilray&#8217;s Common Stock at their option, at any time, until the close of business on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">second</em>&#160;scheduled trading day immediately before&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2027.&#160;</em>The initial conversion rate is approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142764347" contextRef="d_2023-05-30_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">37.66</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares per&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764348" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="tlry:DebtInstrumentConvertibleMultiplesOfPrincipalAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;principal amount of TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, which represents a conversion price of approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764350" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">26.55</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes are now&#160;redeemable, in whole and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;in part, at Tilray&#8217;s option at any time on or after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2025&#160;</em>at a cash redemption price equal to the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date, but only if the last reported sale price of Tilray&#8217;s Common Stock exceeds&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142764353" contextRef="d_2023-05-30_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleThresholdPercentageOfStockPriceTrigger" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">130</ix:nonFraction>% of the conversion price for a specified period of time. If certain corporate events that constitute a fundamental change occur, then, subject to a limited exception, noteholders&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>require&#160;Tilray&#160;to repurchase their TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date. In connection with the Company&#8217;s offering of the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, the Company entered into a share lending agreement with an affiliate of&#160;Jefferies LLC&#160;(the &#8220;Share Borrower&#8221;), pursuant to which it lent&#160;to the Share Borrower <ix:nonFraction id="c142764356" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:OwnshareLendingArrangementSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,850,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock (the &#8220;Borrowed Shares&#8221;). The Borrowed Shares were newly-issued shares,&#160;will be held as treasury shares until the expiration or early termination of the share lending agreement&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be used by purchasers of the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes&#160;to sell up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142764358" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:OwnshareLendingArrangementSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,850,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock. The fair value of the share lending agreement has been recorded as part of the unamortized discount on the debenture. The Company expects that the selling stockholders will use their position created by such sales to establish their initial hedge with respect to their investments in the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes. The Company did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;receive any proceeds from the sale of the Borrowed Shares.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, the Company granted <ix:nonFraction id="c142764473" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28_AwardTypeAxis-TimebasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4,554,321</ix:nonFraction> time-based Restricted Stock Units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">During the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024, </em>the Company issued (i) <ix:nonFraction id="c142764474" contextRef="d_2023-06-01_2024-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformancebasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">756,615</ix:nonFraction> performance&#8209;based restricted stock units (the &#8220;Performance&#8209;Based RSUs&#8221;) and (ii) an additional performance&#8209;based award payable in cash or, at the discretion of the Company&#8217;s Compensation Committee, in shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock (the &#8220;Performance&#8209;Based Elective Settlement Award,&#8221; and together with the Performance&#8209;Based RSUs, the &#8220;Performance&#8209;Based Awards&#8221;). The Performance&#8209;Based Awards were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered granted for accounting purposes at the time of issuance because the applicable performance conditions had <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet been established or approved. Accordingly, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> compensation expense was recognized within the Consolidated Statements of Loss at that time. During the period from issuance through the quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026, </em>the number of outstanding Performance&#8209;Based RSUs was reduced from <ix:nonFraction id="c142767592" contextRef="i_2025-11-30_AwardTypeAxis-PerformancebasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsOutstandingNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">756,615</ix:nonFraction> to <ix:nonFraction id="c142764478" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_AwardTypeAxis-PerformancebasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsOutstandingNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">744,117</ix:nonFraction> as a result of employee attrition, and the Performance&#8209;Based Elective Settlement Awards were also correspondingly reduced.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the Company established and approved the relevant performance conditions for the Performance&#8209;Based Awards and, as a result, the awards were considered granted for accounting purposes. Beginning in the quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2025, </em>the Company commenced recognition of stock&#8209;based compensation expense based on the grant&#8209;date fair value of the Performance&#8209;Based Awards, which is being recognized over the remaining requisite service period. The Company currently expects the Performance&#8209;Based Elective Settlement Award to be settled in shares of common stock. Moreover, because the Performance&#8209;Based Elective Settlement Award has a fixed monetary value and is settleable in a variable number of shares, it is classified as a liability within the statement of Financial Position. The Performance&#8209;Based RSUs are classified as equity awards and are reflected within stockholders&#8217; equity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s total stock-based compensation expense incurred for&#160;the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764483" contextRef="d_2025-12-01_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">13,725</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764484" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">31,060</ix:nonFraction>&#160;compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764485" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">4,035</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764486" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">18,189</ix:nonFraction> for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28,</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">All current and prior year share amounts have been retrospectively adjusted to reflect the Reverse Stock Split, which became effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2, 2025.&#160;</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17.</em> Income taxes</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">The determination of the Company&#8217;s overall effective&#160;tax&#160;rate requires significant judgment, the use of estimates, and the interpretation and application of complex&#160;tax&#160;laws. The effective&#160;tax&#160;rate reflects the income earned and taxed in various United States federal, state, and foreign jurisdictions.&#160;Tax&#160;law changes, increases, and decreases in temporary and permanent differences between book and&#160;tax&#160;items, valuation allowances against the deferred tax assets, stock compensation, and the Company&#8217;s change in income in each jurisdiction all affect the overall effective&#160;tax&#160;rate. It is the Company&#8217;s practice to recognize interest and penalties related to uncertain&#160;tax&#160;positions in income&#160;tax&#160;expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company reported income tax expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764688" contextRef="d_2025-12-01_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,974</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764689" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,235</ix:nonFraction> for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764692" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,203</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764693" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">4,125</ix:nonFraction> for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28,</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The income tax expense&#160;in the current period varies from the US statutory income tax rate and prior year period primarily due to the geographical mix of earnings and losses with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> tax benefit resulting from valuation allowances in certain jurisdictions.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 25pt;"><i>Legal proceedings</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the ordinary course of business, we are at times subject to various legal proceedings and disputes, including the proceedings specifically discussed below. We assess our liabilities and contingencies in connection with outstanding legal proceedings utilizing the latest information available. Where it is probable that we will incur a loss and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated, we record a liability in our consolidated financial statements. These legal reserves&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be increased or decreased to reflect any relevant developments on a quarterly basis. Where a loss is&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;probable or the amount of loss is&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;estimable, we do&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;accrue legal reserves. While the outcome of legal proceedings is inherently uncertain, based on information currently available and available insurance coverage, our management believes that it has established appropriate legal reserves. Any incremental liabilities arising from pending legal proceedings are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;expected to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position, consolidated results of operations, or consolidated cash flows. However, it is possible that the ultimate resolution of these matters, if unfavorable,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be material to our consolidated financial position, consolidated results of operations, or consolidated cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>MMIRF, LLC v. Tilray Brands, Inc., et al.</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>MMIRF, LLC filed a complaint in the Superior Court of California, Los Angeles County, against Tilray Brands, Inc., Serruya Private Equity Inc., Superhero Acquisition Corp., Superhero Acquisition L.P., Irwin Simon, Michael Serruya, and Denise Faltischek, asserting claims for breach of fiduciary duty, aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty, and civil conspiracy against all defendants.&#160;The plaintiff allegedly is an assignee of claims previously possessed by MM CAN USA, Inc., a former subsidiary of MedMen Enterprises, Inc. (&#8220;MedMen&#8221;).&#160;The complaint alleges that, following a series of transactions in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2021 </em>pursuant to which Tilray (and other investors) acquired an interest in senior secured convertible notes of MedMen through its investment in Superhero Acquisition L.P. as a limited partner (as previously disclosed in a current report filed on Form <em style="font: inherit;">8</em>-K on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 17, 2021), </em>Tilray and the other defendants gained &#8220;de facto&#8221; control over, and thereby became fiduciaries of, MedMen.&#160;The complaint further alleges that the defendants breached those purported fiduciary duties in taking certain actions that detrimentally impacted MedMen&#8217;s business, which ultimately entered bankruptcy and receivership proceedings in <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2024. </em>The plaintiff seeks damages in excess of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764710" contextRef="d_2025-12-31_2025-12-31_LitigationCaseAxis-MmirfLlcVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-PendingLitigationMember_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-DamagesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-9">1.0</ix:nonFraction> billion. The defendants&#8217; deadline to move, answer, or otherwise respond to the complaint is currently <em style="font: inherit;"> March 30, 2026. </em>Tilray intends to vigorously defend against the claims asserted in the complaint.&#160;Based on the information available as of the date of this Quarterly Report, management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe that a loss is probable or reasonably estimable, and accordingly <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> accrual has been recorded.</p>
   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Summary of litigation accruals&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">As described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>&#160;(Accounts payable and accrued liabilities), the total estimated litigation&#160;expense accrual included in accrued liabilities as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025&#160;</em>was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764714" contextRef="i_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">11,931</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764715" contextRef="i_2025-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">12,431</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. During the intervening period, the accrual decreased by $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764716" contextRef="d_2025-12-01_2026-02-28_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-SettledClaimsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualCarryingValuePeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4" sign="-">410</ix:nonFraction> from settled claims and decreased&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142764717" contextRef="d_2025-12-01_2026-02-28_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-ChangeInEstimatedLikelihoodOfClaimsSettlementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualCarryingValuePeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4" sign="-">90</ix:nonFraction> due to a net change in the estimated likelihood of certain claim&#8217;s settlement, with the remaining change attributable to foreign exchange effects. This estimated accrual is intended to cover various ongoing litigation matters with probable losses that can be reasonably estimated.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 25pt;text-indent:-25pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">24.</em> Financial risk management and financial instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Financial instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company's classification of its financial instruments is described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;(Significant accounting policies) in the Notes to our Annual Financial Statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The carrying values of marketable securities, accounts receivable, bank indebtedness and accounts payable and accrued liabilities approximate their fair values due to their short periods to maturity.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, the Company had long-term debt of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764986" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LongtermDebtExcludingConvertibleDebenturesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongtermDebtPercentageBearingFixedInterestAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,047</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764987" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LongtermDebtExcludingConvertibleDebenturesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongtermDebtPercentageBearingFixedInterestAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,546</ix:nonFraction>, respectively,&#160;and the principal portion of convertible debentures payable of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764988" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">100,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142764989" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">105,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively,&#160;subject to fixed interest rates. The Company&#8217;s long-term debt is valued based on discounting the future cash outflows associated with the long-term debt. The discount rate is based on the incremental premium above market rates for the U.S. Department of the Treasury securities of similar duration. In each period thereafter, the incremental premium is held constant while the U.S. Department of the Treasury security is based on the then current market value to derive the discount rate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

As a result of lower&#8209;than&#8209;anticipated sales volumes during the peak selling periods of <em style="font: inherit;"> June, </em><em style="font: inherit;"> July </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2025, </em>and the&#160;loss of certain national retail programs, management concluded that Montauk <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer had a viable path to achieving the sales volume target or the&#160;EBITDA target&#160;within the earn&#8209;out period. Accordingly, the Company applied a probability of achievement of <ix:nonFraction id="c142765005" contextRef="i_2025-08-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AcquisitionOfMontaukBrewingCompanyIncMember_MeasurementInputTypeAxis-MeasurementInputProbabilityOfSalesTargetAchievementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiabilityMeasurementInput" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>% to the sales volume target and <ix:nonFraction id="c142765007" contextRef="i_2025-08-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AcquisitionOfMontaukBrewingCompanyIncMember_MeasurementInputTypeAxis-MeasurementInputProbabilityOfRemainingAchievementsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiabilityMeasurementInput" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>% to the remaining criteria. The resulting $<ix:nonFraction id="c142765008" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-08-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AcquisitionOfMontaukBrewingCompanyIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationArrangementsChangeInAmountOfContingentConsiderationLiability1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6" sign="-">15,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;change in fair value of the contingent consideration liability was recorded within the statement of profit and&#160;loss&#160;and&#160;contributed&#160;to the Company&#8217;s&#160;net income generated during the period ended <em style="font: inherit;"> August 31, 2025, </em>despite historically reporting a net loss.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, the earn-out period concluded and neither financial measure was achieved. Accordingly, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142765010">no</span> further changes to&#160;the fair value of the contingent consideration liability were recognized during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026&#160;</em>as <ix:nonFraction id="c142765012" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AcquisitionOfMontaukBrewingCompanyIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiability" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> contingent consideration obligation was&#160;payable.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">The fair value measurement was&#160;based on significant unobservable inputs related to projected operating performance and expected cash outflows and was therefore classified was a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company&#8217;s prepaids and other current assets, long lived assets, including property and equipment, assets held for sale, goodwill and intangible assets are measured at fair value when there is an indicator of impairment and are recorded at fair value only when an impairment charge is recognized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Capital and liquidity&#160;management</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Management reviews its capital management approach on an ongoing basis and believes that this approach, given the relative size of the Company, is reasonable. There have been <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> changes to the Company&#8217;s capital management approach in the period. The Company considers its cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities as capital.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2026-02-28" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3152961" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 25pt;text-indent:-25pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">25.</em></b> <b>Segment reporting</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Our Company&#8217;s Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) is the Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer. The&#160;CODM uses segment gross profit for the purpose of resource allocation, assessment of segment performance against determined targets, and in deciding whether to implement cost saving targets. The Company operates in&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142765175">four</span>&#160;segments.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) cannabis operations, which encompasses the production, distribution,&#160;sale, co-manufacturing and advisory services of both medical and adult-use cannabis,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) beverage operations, which encompasses the production, marketing and sale of beverage products,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) distribution operations, which encompasses the purchase and resale of pharmaceuticals products to customers, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">4</em>) wellness products, which encompasses wellness and better-for-you foods and beverages. This structure is in line with how our CODM assesses our performance and allocates resources.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Operating segments have&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;been aggregated and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;asset information is provided for the segments because the Company&#8217;s CODM does&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;receive asset information by segment on a regular basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">The following tables reconcile the Company&#8217;s segment gross profit&#160;to consolidated U.S. GAAP results:</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Company Overview </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Tilray Brands, Inc., a Delaware corporation (collectively, along with its subsidiaries, the &#8220;Company&#8221;, &#8220;Tilray&#8221;, &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221; and &#8220;our&#8221;),&#160;is a leading global lifestyle&#160;consumer products company, which was incorporated on January 24, 2018 and is headquartered in Leamington and New York, with operations in Canada, the United States, Europe, Australia and Latin America&#160;that is leading as a transformative force at the nexus of cannabis, beverage, wellness, and entertainment, elevating lives through moments of connection. Tilray&#8217;s mission is to be a leading premium lifestyle company with a house of brands and&#160;innovative products that inspire joy, wellness and create memorable experiences.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Our overall strategy is to leverage our brands, infrastructure, expertise and capabilities to drive revenue growth&#160;in the industries in which we compete, achieve industry-leading&#160;profitability&#160;and build sustainable, long-term shareholder value. In order to ensure the long-term sustainable growth of our Company, we continue to focus on developing strong capabilities in data analytics and consumer insights,&#160;drive category management leadership and assess opportunities for&#160;the introduction of new categories, products and entries into new geographies. In addition, we are relentlessly focused on managing our cost structure and expenses in order to maintain our strong financial position. Finally, our experienced leadership team provides a strong foundation to accelerate our growth. Our management team is complemented by experienced operators, cannabis industry experts, veteran beer and beverage industry leaders and leaders that are well-established in wellness and better-for-you products, all of whom apply an innovative and consumer-centric approach to our businesses.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 25pt;"><i><b>Beverage&#160;market trends: </b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Within the beverage category,&#160;we expect the following key trends to continue to shape the near-term outlook&#160;in this segment:</p>
  <div style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">
   <div style="font-size: 10pt;">

Through targeted efforts, we continue to&#160;strategically optimize our price/pack/channel architecture and drive distribution to continue to execute against our craft beer strategy, streamlining our business, enhancing our relevance and focusing resources on our core markets. The 2026 preliminary Spring retail resets&#160;resulted in innovation gains in emerging categories.</p> </td>

Our other innovative products include Hemp Derived Delta-9 (HD-D9) beverages. Although new U.S. federal legislation was recently enacted that will restrict the production and sale of our HD&#8209;D9 beverages beginning in November 2026, we believe that new regulations could evolve prior to that date to permit continued sales of HD-D9 beverages. These strategic innovations underscore our commitment to offering high-quality options across a diverse range of beverage categories, positioning us for sustained growth by meeting consumer demand and differentiation in the competitive beverage segment.</p> </td>

    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">In the spirits category, Breckenridge Distillery combines premium craftsmanship, award-winning quality, and experiential tourism appeal, reinforcing its niche as a lifestyle-driven spirits brand. Recently included in Newsweek's &#8220;Best Bourbon 2026&#8221; list, the distillery has earned multiple prestigious accolades across Whiskey, Gin, and Vodka, including three Icons of Whisky awards, ten Best American Blended Whiskey honors at the World Whiskies Awards, and recognition as Colorado Distillery of the Year.&#160;Breckenridge Distillery products are available in all 50 states, with continued planned expansion and product innovations. Despite prevailing challenges within the overall spirits market, we believe our focus on whiskey&#8212;a resilient segment&#8212;combined with our award-winning portfolio and innovative product introductions, positions Breckenridge Distillery for sustained growth and enhanced market presence.</p>

    <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;"><b><i>Canadian cannabis market trends:</i></b></p>
    <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   </div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">The cannabis industry in Canada continues&#160;to evolve given how nascent the industry is with federal legalization of adult-use cannabis occurring just over five years ago. Through analysis of the current market conditions, the following key trends have emerged and are anticipated to influence the near-term future in the Canadian cannabis&#160;industry:</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">
   <tbody>
    <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
     <td style="width: 27pt;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Market share</i>. During the fiscal quarter, Tilray continued&#160;to lead the Canadian market with the highest cannabis revenue in Canada. However, during the fiscal quarter, we experienced a decrease in market share in Canada from 9.3% to 8.5%&#160;from the immediately preceding quarter&#160;as reported by Hifyre data for all provinces, excluding Quebec where Weedcrawler was deemed more accurate. The decline primarily reflected a 175 basis point decrease in the whole flower category resulting from a planned cultivation strain rotation that temporarily impacted supply, and a 728 basis point decrease in the straight-edge pre&#8209;roll category due to an out&#8209;of&#8209;stock experienced by a componentry vendor despite maintaining a&#160;market leading&#160;position within this category. These declines were partially offset by a 547 basis point increase in the blunts category. The Company continues to enhance its global supply chain and expand its cultivation footprint to support demand across Canadian and international markets. During the fiscal quarter ended February 28, 2025, the Company opportunistically redirected approximately 0.8&#160;Metric&#160;Tons&#160;to international markets, which are expected to generate higher margin sales.</p> </td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Consumer preferences and Price compression.</i>&#160;Licensed producer consolidation has progressed more gradually than anticipated, while retailer consolidation has increased the negotiating leverage of larger retailer accounts.&#160;At the same time, consumer preferences continue to evolve. Demand is shifting toward manufactured formats such as infused pre&#8209;rolls, beverages, edibles, and vapes, reflecting a broader premiumization and convenience trend within the category. Historical price compression in specific categories is expected to persist&#160;in the market, intensified by fierce competition among the approximately 1,000 Licensed Producers in Canada. The fixed impact of excise per gram, notwithstanding the decline in average selling prices, further compounds these challenges, and has promoted ongoing industry lobbying efforts.&#160;</p> </td>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><i><b>International cannabis trends:</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">We are a global leader in the development, production, distribution, marketing and sale of pharmaceutical-grade medical cannabis products.&#160;The cannabis industry in Europe is still in its early stages of development and countries within Europe are at different stages of medical cannabis legalization. Meaningful progress in the legalization and regulation of cannabis for medical purposes, has now taken place in more than 21&#160;countries representing a population of more than 526 million people (Germany, UK, Italy, Poland, Netherlands, Czech Republic, Greece, Portugal, Austria, Switzerland, Denmark, Croatia, Malta, Luxembourg, Ukraine, Sweden, Norway,&#160;T&#252;rkiye, Ireland, Spain and Israel). Beyond this, some countries have expressed a clear political ambition to legalize adult-use cannabis (Portugal&#160;and Luxembourg), some are engaging in programs for adult-use legalization (Germany, Netherlands, Malta, Czech Republic and Switzerland) and some are debating regulations for cannabinoid-based medicine (France). In Europe, we believe that, despite continuing recessionary economic conditions, political uncertainty in various countries and the continuing Russian conflict with Ukraine, cannabis legalization (both medicinal and adult-use) will continue to gain traction albeit more slowly than originally expected. This is evidenced by the cannabis regulations in Germany adopted on April 1, 2024, which we believe will serve as a catalyst for continued changes in drug policy throughout Europe.&#160;Outside of Europe and North America, the cannabis industry is also continuing to develop&#160;with Australia representing one of the larger markets and with some Latin American countries also growing their respective medical cannabis markets, such as Argentina, Panama, Colombia and Brazil.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">We continue to believe that Tilray remains uniquely well-positioned to maintain and gain significant market share in the markets in which we participate. We benefit from our end-to-end vertically-integrated infrastructure in major markets and well-placed investments, which are comprised of two EU-GMP cultivation facilities located in Portugal and Germany; our fully owned route-to-market encompassing sales, marketing and distribution infrastructure in Germany, Australia and Italy; a network of leading distributors who we work with in the various other countries in which we participate; and, our extensive genetics portfolio and demonstrated commitment and expertise related to the cultivation and production of high-quality, safe cannabis products.&#160; Tilray&#8217;s International business also benefits from the depth and breadth of knowledge, experience, relationships and infrastructure we have gleaned from our leading participation and investment into the Canadian medical and adult-use markets. Tilray is proudly pioneering the effort to further understand the therapeutic value of cannabis through&#160;strategic partnerships with leading research institutions globally where&#160;Tilray is currently supporting clinical trials around the world studying the efficacy of cannabis in treading various indications. We believe that these assets and attributes, combined with our ability to navigate complex regulatory environments, will continue to drive our leadership in international medical markets and allow us to successfully enter new markets as they adopt medical cannabis and potentially adult-use regulations and may also serve to support a potential U.S. participation.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Germany</i>. Today, Germany remains the largest medical cannabis market in Europe.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">We continue to believe that Tilray is well-positioned in Germany, especially considering the enactment of MedCanG and given that we are one of only three manufacturers of medical cannabis in Germany since our wholly owned subsidiary, Aphria RX, was awarded the first&#160;license for the cultivation of medical cannabis in Germany by the BfArM under the liberalized regime. Said license improves our ability to meet the needs of patients and provides cannabis of the utmost quality and enhanced availability to a broader market.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">As the market continues to mature, we have seen increased demands and differentiation specifically with medical cannabis flowers. In response, we have launched&#160;ARX&#160;and Good Supply brands and related medical cannabis products, which provides the patient with a segmented portfolio of products while we continue to deliver on the trust, safety and consistency that has become expected from our Tilray Medical brand.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Poland</i>.&#160;In Poland, cannabis was legalized for medical use in 2018 and&#160;is prescribed to patients by a physician and dispensed by pharmacies.&#160;Today, all doctors in Poland are allowed to prescribe medical cannabis and it is a self-pay&#160;market as medical cannabis is not refundable by the Polish health service. Tilray is a leading supplier of medical cannabis in Poland through our network of distributor partnerships.&#160;We predominantly supply the market with whole flower medical cannabis products.&#160; &#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>United Kingdom</i>.&#160;Since November 2018, doctors in the UK have been able to prescribe medical cannabis for medicinal use for patients with medical conditions that had failed to respond to first-line medications.&#160; The market today is predominantly all self-pay and prescriptions are facilitated by private clinics.&#160;Today, we supply the UK market with mainly whole flower products from&#160;brands such as Good Supply through our distributor partners with sights on growing our portfolio to extracts and other formats.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Ireland. </i>In June 2019, the Minister for Health signed legislation allowing for the operation of the Medical Cannabis Access Programme (&#8220;MCAP&#8221;) on a pilot basis for five years. The MCAP allows a medical consultant to prescribe a cannabis-based treatment for a narrow set of specified medical conditions, where the patient has failed to respond to standard treatment. Reimbursement is available for products which have received the appropriate approvals. Tilray was one of the first players to enter the Irish market and is one of a few suppliers which has received approval for its products to be prescribed and to have been granted reimbursement status. Today, we supply our approved extract product to Ireland through our distribution partner.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Italy</i>.&#160;In May 2023, Tilray Medical received authorization from Italy&#8217;s Ministry of Health to distribute three new medical cannabis compounds. These medical cannabis compounds are distributed by Tilray medical Italia&#160;to pharmacies across Italy.&#160;We have an established broad national pharmaceutical distribution network in Italy, where medical cannabis is prescribed by doctors and reimbursed by the healthcare system to eligible patients.&#160;In 2025, Tilray has received additional cannabis flower and extract product authorizations and has formed a strategic partnership with Molteni Farmaceutici with the commitment to broaden the availability of Tilray Medical products for patients across Italy.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Australia</i>. In 2016, the Australian Government legalized medicinal cannabis, which is regulated by the Therapeutic Goods Administration.&#160;Medical cannabis is prescribed by a doctor but there is no coverage under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.&#160;Tilray Medical supplies the market with a wide portfolio of medical cannabis extracts as well as whole flower products.&#160;As the market continues to mature, we have seen increased demands and differentiation specifically with medical cannabis flowers. In response, we launched the Broken Coast, Redecan and Good Supply brands and products, which provides the patient with a segmented portfolio of products while we continue to deliver on the trust, safety and consistency that has become expected from our Tilray Medical brand.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Luxembourg</i>. Luxembourg established its medical cannabis framework in 2018, with the national program&#160;operational since February 2019. Medical cannabis is tightly regulated, accessible only through trained physicians and dispensed exclusively via hospital pharmacies. Prescriptions are limited to patients with defined, severe medical conditions, and all treatments are covered by public health insurance. In January 2025, Luxembourg updated its regulations to phase-out high-THC flower products, now permitting only balanced or high-CBD flower and oil-based extracts. This shift reflects the government&#8217;s commitment to standardized, pharmaceutical-grade cannabis therapies and patient safety. Tilray Deutschland GmbH was awarded the official government tender in 2025 to supply medical cannabis flower, demonstrating our leadership in centralized procurement and compliance with Luxembourg&#8217;s rigorous standards.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Portugal</i>. Portugal legalized medical cannabis in July 2018. The regulatory framework is overseen by INFARMED, requiring Market Placement Authorization (ACM) for all non-pharmaceutical cannabis products, with strict GACP and GMP compliance. While domestic patient access remains limited due to stringent product approvals and the absence of public reimbursement, Portugal has emerged as a leading European producer and exporter of medical cannabis, supplying high-value markets such as Germany, Poland, and Australia. In 2021, Tilray received the first Authorization for Placement on the Market for dried flower, with additional product approvals in 2024, reinforcing our pioneering role in Portugal&#8217;s medical cannabis sector. Our strategic investments in cultivation and manufacturing, combined with robust compliance and documentation standards, enable Tilray to deliver EU-GMP quality products to both domestic and international markets. As Portugal explores adult-use reform, we expect that Tilray&#8217;s established reputation and operational excellence position us to capitalize on future regulatory developments and market expansion.</p>
