  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;"><i><b>Wellness market trends: </b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Tilray Wellness&#8217;s branded business continues to grow across brick-and-mortar retail as well as ecommerce, which we believe further establishes&#160;its leading market share position in better-for-you categories.&#160;The Company&#160;continues to focus on value-added innovation within natural and organic food and beverages across branded and ingredient sales. We continue to&#160;participate&#160;in multiple growing categories including super-seeds, better for you breakfast, better for you snacking, and natural energy drinks.&#160;Within our Ingredients sales business, we have expanded our range of offerings in hemp protein and hemp oil, helping us further develop our business in North America and Asia.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Acquisitions, Strategic Transactions and Synergies</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">We strive to continue to expand our business, on a consolidated basis, through a combination of organic growth and acquisition. While we continue to execute against our strategic initiatives that we believe will result in&#160;long-term, sustainable growth and value to our stockholders, we continue to evaluate potential acquisitions and other strategic transactions of businesses that we believe complement our existing portfolio, infrastructure and capabilities or provide us with the opportunity to enter attractive new geographic markets and product categories as well as expand our existing capabilities. In addition, we have exited certain businesses and continue to evaluate certain businesses within our portfolio that are dilutive to profitability and cash flow. As a result, we incur transaction costs in connection with identifying and completing acquisitions and strategic transactions, as well as ongoing integration and restructuring costs as we combine acquired companies and continue to achieve synergies, which is offset by income generated in connection with the execution of these transactions. For the&#160;nine months ended February 28, 2026, we incurred&#160;$2.9&#160;million of transaction expenses, as discussed further below in the results of operations assessment.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>BrewDog Acquisitions:</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>&#160;</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Subsequent to the period ended February 28, 2026, on March 2, 2026, Tilray UK, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into the BrewDog BASA. Under the BrewDog BASA, Tilray UK acquired certain business operations and assets of BrewDog plc and certain of its subsidiary undertakings (collectively, the &#8220;BrewDog Group&#8221;) through a pre-packaged administration process in Scotland under the Insolvency Act 1986, with the intent for Tilray UK to carry on the acquired business operations and assets as a going concern. The assets acquired included&#160;the UK Brewery, the online business, the retail business, 11 of the BrewDog strategic brewpubs in Scotland, England and Ireland and all the intellectual property rights relating to the BrewDog brand, including well known sub-brands such as Punk IPA, Hazy Jane, Wingman, Elvis Juice and Dead Pony Club. The purchase price was &#163;33.0 million&#160;(approximately $44.1 million).&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">In a separate transaction completed on March 9, 2026, the Company acquired BrewDog Brewing Australia Pty Ltd., which included BrewDog&#8217;s Australian brewery, along with two hospitality venues in Australia for a nominal consideration.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">On March 16, 2026, Tilray BrewDog U.S., Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into an asset purchase agreement to acquire certain strategic BrewDog assets in the U.S., including a brewery, pub, and hotel in Columbus, Ohio, as well as pubs located in New Albany, Ohio, Cleveland, Ohio, and Las Vegas, Nevada. The purchase price for BrewDog&#8217;s U.S. assets is equal to $9.3 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">On March 23, 2026, the Company acquired 5&#160;additional BrewDog&#160;brewpubs in Scotland and&#160;England for a purchase price of &#163;0.3 million&#160;(approximately $0.5 million). See Note 26 (Subsequent Events).&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">One of the world&#8217;s most recognized names in craft beer, BrewDog is a brand-powered, vertically integrated beverage and hospitality platform.&#160;Founded in 2007, BrewDog quickly became one of the largest independent craft beer brands in the United Kingdom with its portfolio of iconic craft, premium and low and&#160;no alcohol beer brands, including Punk IPA, Hazy Jane, Lost Lager and Wingman.&#160;From its beginnings in the UK, it developed its strong global brand awareness through its global expansion via international breweries, localized brewpubs and strategic partnerships.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">These acquisitions present an important step for the Company as it executes against its previously announced strategic initiative to expand its beverage platform into the international markets, The strong global awareness of the BrewDog brand, together with its international brewing infrastructure and experiential pubs, presents an opportunity for growth in the UK, Europe and previously untapped international markets, including the Asia Pacific region.&#160;Further, the acquisition of the BrewDog U.S. aligns with our &#8220;regional jewel&#8221; strategy as BrewDog has built a strong brand in Ohio, which supports and strengthens our presence in the Midwest and provides us with a highly visible presence in Las Vegas, including a flagship brewpub located on a premier stretch of the Las Vegas Strip.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><b><i>Beverage segment Project 420:&#160;</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">In November 2020, we entered the beverage category with the acquisition of SweetWater Brewing Company, one of the largest independent craft brewers in the U.S. by volume, with the vision of creating a more diversified global lifestyle consumer products company.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">This initial acquisition provided us with a foundation to pursue additional acquisitions in the beverage category and scale our business on a national basis. We acquired Alpine Beer Company, Green Flash and Breckenridge Distillery in December 2021, Montauk Brewing Company in November 2022, Craft Acquisition I in October 2023 and Craft Acquisition II in September 2024.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">With Craft Acquisition I and Craft Acquisition II, we capitalized on opportunities to acquire additional beverage businesses that consisted of strong brands in decline due to lack of focus and in need of investment in order to promote growth, all at a significantly reduced purchase price. To support the growth of these acquired brands and establish a clear path to profitability, we implemented Project 420, which is a comprehensive plan covering (i) SKU optimization/rationalization; (ii) Geographic rationalization; (iii) Distributor rationalization; and&#160;(iv) synergy optimization plan through which we expect to invest in the acquired brands for growth and improve profitability:</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">
   <tbody>
    <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
     <td style="width: 27pt; padding: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="width: 18pt; padding: 0pt; text-align: justify;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto; text-align: justify; padding: 0pt; font-size: 10pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">SKU optimization/rationalization</span>&#160;</i>&#8211;<i>&#160;</i>In response to the declining growth in the craft beer industry and consolidation of distributors, we are working with our distributors in various markets to streamline our portfolio by eliminating duplicative, lower margin and slower growth products, which has the immediate effect of reducing revenue. However, by eliminating these slower moving and lower margin SKUs, we are able to focus our attention and resources on our higher margin and faster growing SKUs, as well as the introduction of new innovation, which we expect will accelerate our revenue growth in future quarters.&#160;</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">
   <tbody>
    <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
     <td style="width: 27pt;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Geographic rationalization</span> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>On a consolidated basis, we generate sales in all states however, our brands&#160;are significantly stronger in their home markets.&#160;For example, SweetWater is located in Georgia and, as a result, its revenues are stronger in Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina and Florida, while 10 Barrel, which is located in Oregon has stronger revenue in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and Wyoming.&#160;In away markets, like Oregon for SweetWater, and Georgia for 10 Barrel, the brands are not as strong and so distribution is de-empathized.&#160;Our geographic rationalization works to concentrate our efforts in individual states with our strongest brands in those states.&#160;As we reduce the distribution of away markets brands in those states, we are working to increase the distribution and shelf space of home market brands.&#160;This initiative is consistent with our Regional Jewel strategy developed in conjunction with the Boston Consulting Group two years ago.</p> </td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt;">

    <tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

     <td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Distributor rationalization</span> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>As a result of our various acquisitions in the last five years, we have over 750 distributors and 975 distributor shipping locations. As a result, we are shipping to multiple distributors in the same geography as well as splitting the allocation of local brands between multiple distributors. The goal of the distributor rationalization is to reduce our distributor footprint down to between 450 and 500 distributors, concentrating those distributors&#8217; effort on our brands and SKUs, while minimizing logistical complexities.</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Synergy optimization plan</span> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>We previously announced a $33.0 million synergy plan focused on optimizing our production footprint and eliminating redundancies in manufacturing and warehouse assets.&#160;By integrating the newly acquired facilities into our existing footprint, we are optimizing capacities, utilization and better absorbing fixed overheads. This in turn is improving our gross margins. As of the fiscal quarter ended February 28, 2026, we&#160;have completed the synergy optimization plan achieving the $33.0 million target.&#160;While this initiative is complete, management remains focused on disciplined cost management and continues to advance additional cost&#8209;saving initiatives across the business to drive further margin improvement and operating efficiency.</p> </td>
    </tr>

Our intention is to fund this investment through the cost savings and synergies achieved through Project 420.</p> </td>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">It is important to note, however, that there is a lag between the discontinuation of the SKUs and the associated reduction in revenue, which has an immediate effect, and the acceleration of the growth of our existing SKUs and the introduction of new innovation and the associated increase in revenue, which takes time due to retailer resets.&#160;We also expect these efforts will lead to improved sales and margins, with benefits realized through lower selling costs, as well as reduced requirements for working capital through inventory reductions and an improvement in our cash conversion cycle.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Political and Economic Environment</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Our results of operations may continue to be affected by economic, political, legislative, regulatory, legal actions, global volatility and general market disruption resulting from&#160;geopolitical tensions, such as Russia's continued incursion into Ukraine,&#160;the ongoing events in the Middle East, including the conflict involving Iran, and political uncertainty in certain countries in Europe.&#160;Escalation of hostilities in the Middle East, including involving Iran, could further disrupt global energy markets, fuel prices, transportation networks, and supply chains, particularly in Europe, which may indirectly impact operating costs and consumer demand. Economic conditions, such as recessionary trends, inflation, supply chain disruptions, interest and monetary exchange rates, government fiscal policies, and the recent economic uncertainties resulting from&#160;certain changes in U.S. global economic policy, including changes on global trade policies can have a significant effect on operations. More specifically, there are no expected impacts on revenue from the recently enacted U.S. tariffs and foreign enacted retaliatory&#160;tariffs (&#8220;Tariffs&#8221;). From a cost perspective, we believe the recently enacted Tariffs could impact input materials such as aluminum, hops, barley, malt and vape componentry, which are partially imported&#160;but we intend to mitigate these impacts to the extent&#160;possible.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">In addition,&#160;U.S. federal regulatory developments regarding cannabis rescheduling represent a significant shift in the political and legislative environment.&#160;This regulatory evolution is expected to create a more credible framework for medical cannabis research, clinical development, and compliance, aligning with Tilray&#8217;s established global expertise in regulated medical cannabis markets; although, there are no assurances whether such rescheduling will be implemented as and when anticipated. The Company intends to leverage its proven compliance infrastructure, scientific knowledge, and operational scale to expand responsibly in the U.S. market, introducing medical-grade cannabis products in targeted therapeutic formats. While these developments present significant long-term growth opportunities, they also introduce new regulatory complexities and potential risks that we will continue to monitor closely.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Reverse Stock Split</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Effective December 2, 2025, we implemented a Reverse Stock Split of our outstanding shares of Common Stock, at a ratio of one-for-ten.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">No fractional shares were issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Fractional shares resulting from the Reverse Stock Split were rounded down to the nearest whole share and stockholders received cash in lieu of any fractional shares that were created by the Reverse Stock Split, see Note 14 (Stockholder&#8217;s equity) for additional details. Each stockholder's percentage ownership interest in the Company and proportional voting power remained unchanged as a result of the Reverse Stock Split, except for adjustments that resulted from rounding fractional shares down to whole shares.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">All issued and outstanding Common Stock, per share amounts, and outstanding equity instruments and awards exercisable into Common Stock contained in the condensed interim consolidated financial statements of the Company and notes thereto have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the Reverse Stock Split&#160;for all current and prior periods presented.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">These non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, and not in lieu of, the financial measures calculated and presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America, (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). Please see &#8220;Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures to GAAP Measures&#8221; below for reconciliation of such non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, as well as a discussion of our adjusted gross margin, adjusted gross profit and adjusted EBITDA measures and the calculation of such measures.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><i>Constant Currency Presentation</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">We believe that this financial measure provides useful information to investors because it eliminates the effect that foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations may have on period-to-period comparability given the volatility in foreign currency exchange markets and therefore, provides greater transparency to the underlying performance of our consolidated net sales. To present this information for historical periods, current period net sales for entities reporting in currencies other than the U.S. Dollar are translated into U.S. Dollars at the average monthly exchange rate in effect during the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year rather than at the actual average monthly exchange rate in effect during the current period of the current fiscal year. As a result, the foreign currency impact is equal to the current year results in local currencies multiplied by the change in average foreign currency exchange rate between the current fiscal period and the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Cash, restricted cash and Marketable Securities</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company combines the Cash and cash equivalent financial statement line item, the restricted cash financial&#160;statement line&#160;and the Marketable securities financial statement line item as an aggregate total as reconciled in the liquidity and capital resource section below. The Company&#8217;s management believes that this presentation provides useful information to management, analysts and investors regarding certain additional financial and business trends relating to its short-term liquidity position by combining these three&#160;GAAP metrics.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Beverage&#160;revenue </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Net revenue from our Beverage segment&#160;decreased&#160;to&#160;$42.6&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$148.4&#160;million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to revenue of $55.9&#160;million and&#160;$175.0&#160;million for the prior year&#160;periods.&#160;The decline was primarily attributable to continued industry-wide challenges&#160;across the craft beer, spirits, and brewpub categories and broader competitive pressures, which resulted in lower volumes sold. Additionally, the decline was driven in part by margin&#8209;focused actions, which reduced net revenue by approximately $3.0&#160;million and $13.6&#160;million during the three and nine month periods, respectively. Lastly, the HD-D9 category was negatively impacted by U.S. federal legislation that was recently enacted which&#160;will restrict the future production and sale of our HD&#8209;D9 beverages and&#160;reduced net revenue by approximately $1.0&#160;million during the three and nine month periods, respectively.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, these impacts were partially offset by the inclusion of sales from Craft Acquisition II, effective September 1, 2024, which were not reflected in the full&#160;comparative period and would have increased&#160;the nine month revenue for the period ended&#160;February 28, 2025 by approximately $13.6 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Revenue from Canadian medical cannabis: </i></b>Gross revenue from Canadian medical cannabis increased&#160;to $6.0&#160;million and&#160;decreased to&#160;$18.4&#160;million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026&#160;compared to gross revenue of $5.8&#160;million and&#160;$18.8&#160;million for the prior year periods, respectively. On a constant currency basis, gross revenue from Canadian medical cannabis&#160;decreased to&#160;$5.7&#160;million and to&#160;$18.3 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively. The decrease in gross revenue from medical cannabis, on a constant currency basis, was primarily driven by uninsured patient&#160;attrition&#160;to the&#160;adult-use recreational market, which was partially offset by new insured patient acquisition.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><b><i>Revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis: </i></b>During the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, our gross revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis increased&#160;to $52.6&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$179.1 million,&#160;compared to gross revenue of $49.3&#160;million and&#160;$165.6 million for the prior year&#160;periods, respectively. On a constant currency basis,&#160;our gross revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis increased&#160;to $50.2&#160;million and&#160;increased to&#160;$178.4 million&#160;for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively.&#160;The currency adjusted increase in gross adult&#8209;use revenue for the three month period was primarily driven by a $2.7 million increase in the traditional pre&#8209;roll category, reflecting the successful launch of innovation SKUs, including Good Supply Double Dutchies. This growth was partially offset by a $2.1 million decline in the whole flower category, primarily due to the commencement of strain rotation within our cultivation program, which temporarily constrained supply. In addition, certain inventory was redirected to international markets, which would otherwise have generated approximately $0.9 million of revenue in the Canadian market. For the nine month period, the&#160;currency adjusted increase in gross adult&#8209;use revenue was predominantly attributable to a $7.3 million increase in traditional pre&#8209;rolls, driven by the aforementioned product innovations, and a $1.7 million increase in whole flower sales, as the strain rotation did not begin until our&#160;third quarter. Notably, the Company has continued to invest in its cultivation footprint, including the decision to restart cultivation at its Quebec facility, to support growing demand in both the Canadian and international markets. Given the higher margins generally realized on international cannabis sales, the Company may, when advantageous, continue to allocate inventory to international markets, which could negatively impact Canadian adult&#8209;use and wholesale cannabis revenue in future periods as the Company continues to scale its infrastructure.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><b><i>Wholesale cannabis revenue:&#160;</i></b>Gross revenue from wholesale cannabis decreased&#160;to $1.2&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$6.7 million and for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to gross revenue of $3.9&#160;million and&#160;$16.0 million for the prior year&#160;periods respectively. On a constant currency basis, gross revenue from wholesale cannabis&#160;decreased to $1.1&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$6.7 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively. Due to the transition by many licensed producers in the Canadian market to asset-light business models, the Canadian cannabis industry has experienced a reduction in excess inventory resulting in price increases in the B2B market. As a result of this shift in market dynamics and demand, we continue to evaluate the market and may opportunistically sell into the wholesale market&#160;where it makes sense.&#160;Specifically, during the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, wholesale cannabis revenue declined compared to the prior year periods as the Company strategically redirected product to other markets, resulting in a 49% and 47% decrease in wholesale gram equivalents sold, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><b><i>International cannabis revenue:</i></b><b>&#160;</b>Net&#160;revenue from International cannabis&#160;increased&#160;to&#160;$24.1&#160;million and to&#160;$57.7 million&#160;for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to net revenue of $13.9&#160;million and&#160;$41.0 million&#160;for the prior year periods, respectively. On a constant currency&#160;basis, given the strengthening of the Euro against the U.S. Dollar when compared to the prior year quarter, net revenue from international cannabis&#160;increased to&#160;$21.4&#160;million and&#160;increased to&#160;$53.1 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively. The increase in net revenue from International cannabis markets during the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, was primarily attributable to growth in the German medical cannabis market, which increased by $4.0 million and $9.8 million, respectively, the receipt of previously backlogged permits, and an enhanced supply chain. During the three month period, this growth was further supported by a $4.4 million increase in Poland, driven by patient adoption of an in&#8209;person prescription model, and a $1.7 million increase in the United Kingdom through our targeted expansion into emerging markets. Despite increased gram equivalents sold, international cannabis revenue was negatively impacted by price compression of approximately $7.0 million and $16.0 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively. Notwithstanding this pricing pressure, international cannabis sales continue to generate higher margins than Canadian cannabis sales, and the Company remains focused on optimizing its product mix and geographic allocation to maximize profitability.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Distribution</b><b>&#160;revenue </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Net revenue from our Distribution segment&#160;increased&#160;to $83.0&#160;million and&#160;increased to&#160;$242.3 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to revenue of&#160;$61.5&#160;million and&#160;$197.2 million for the prior year periods, respectively. On a constant currency basis, given the change in&#160;the Euro and Argentine Peso against the U.S. Dollar in the fiscal quarter, revenue from Distribution&#160;increased to&#160;$74.0&#160;million and&#160;$223.6 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, respectively. The increase in Distribution revenue for the three month period was primarily driven by a focus on competitive pricing, as evidenced by a 13% increase in average selling price, and a 7% increase in units sold, reflecting greater emphasis on higher&#8209;velocity SKUs, as well as favorable foreign exchange impacts. The increase in Distribution revenue for the nine month period was primarily attributable to a 4% increase in average selling price, an 11% increase in volume, and favorable foreign exchange impacts.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Wellness revenue </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Our Wellness segment net revenue&#160;increased to&#160;$16.4&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$46.2 million for the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026 compared to $14.1&#160;million and&#160;$43.5 million from the prior year periods, respectively. On a constant currency basis for the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, Wellness segment net revenue increased&#160;to&#160;$16.1&#160;million and&#160;to&#160;$46.1&#160;million, respectively. The increase&#160;in revenue was driven by&#160;our strategic focus on value-add innovations, including high protein super-seeds, better-for-you breakfast products, better-for-you snacking, and the continued success of our Hi-Ball clean energy drinks which contributed approximately $0.5 million and $2.6 million of incremental revenue during the three and nine months, respectively. In addition, the acquisition of Blue Sky Hemp Venture&#8217;s customer list&#160;contributed to the growth of our ingredients sales channel by approximately $1.1 million and $3.0 million of incremental revenue during the three and nine month periods, respectively. The remaining Wellness portfolio contributed approximately $0.6 million of revenue growth during the three month period, reflecting improved demand across certain product lines. However, for the nine month period, revenue from the remaining sales channels declined by approximately $2.1 million, primarily due to a shift in one of our supply agreements within the Club retailer channel. We are actively addressing these challenges through targeted initiatives aimed at improving distribution, assortment optimization, and promotional execution&#160;across our Club and Retail sales channels.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Beverage gross margin:</i>&#160;For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, our beverage segment generated gross margin&#160;of&#160;32%&#160;and&#160;34%, respectively, which&#160;decreased from&#160;36%&#160;and&#160;39%&#160;generated in&#160;the&#160;prior year periods, respectively.&#160;Adjusted gross margin&#160;was&#160;32%&#160;and&#160;34%, which&#160;decreased from&#160;36%&#160;and 40%&#160;generated in&#160;the&#160;prior year periods, respectively. The change in the beverage&#160;gross margin and adjusted beverage gross margin for the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026&#160;was driven by several factors, including our Craft Acquisition II, which historically has operated at a lower gross margin of approximately 25%, declining&#160;overhead utilization as our revenue levels have declined, higher input costs and timing delays in realizing the full benefits of our Project 420 cost savings initiatives. Additionally, increased discounting to support sales volume resulted in discounts of 7.2% for the three month period compared to 4.7% in the prior quarter, and 6.6% for the nine month period&#160;compared to 4.1% in the prior year period, which negatively impacted margins and was partially offset by reductions in marketing expenditures.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Cannabis gross margin:</i> For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, our cannabis segment&#160;generated gross margin of&#160;40%&#160;and&#160;38%, respectively, which&#160;decreased from 41%&#160;and remained consistent&#160;at&#160;38% generated in&#160;the prior year periods, respectively.&#160;Although both cannabis net revenue and gross profit increased during the three and nine month periods, gross margin remained largely unchanged. This was primarily due to price compression in international markets, which&#160;negatively impacted international cannabis revenue during the three and nine month periods by approximately $7.0 million and $16.0 million, respectively, despite having increased the gram equivalents sold.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><i>Distribution&#160;gross margin:</i> For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, our distribution segment generated gross margin of&#160;12%&#160;and 12%, respectively, which&#160;increased&#160;from&#160;9%&#160;and&#160;11% generated in&#160;the prior year periods, respectively.&#160;The increase was primarily attributable to a favorable change in product mix, as evidenced by increases in average selling price of approximately 13% and 4% during the three and nine month periods, respectively, as well as initiatives undertaken to reduce input costs.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><i>Wellness gross margin:</i> For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, our wellness segment generated gross margin of&#160;33%&#160;and&#160;32%, respectively, which&#160;increased from&#160;32%&#160;and&#160;31% in the&#160;prior year periods, respectively.&#160;Gross margin remained relatively consistent period over period as strategic price increases largely offset unfavorable changes in sales mix.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">Operating expenses are comprised of general and administrative,&#160;selling, amortization, marketing and promotion, research and development, change in fair value of contingent consideration, impairment of intangible assets and goodwill, other than temporary changes in fair value of convertible notes receivable, litigation&#160;costs, net of recoveries,&#160;restructuring costs and transaction costs (income), net. For the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, operating expenses&#160;decreased by&#160;$730.6 million and&#160;by&#160;$795.2&#160;million to $81.3&#160;million and&#160;$216.5&#160;million when compared to&#160;$811.9&#160;million and&#160;$1,011.7&#160;million for the&#160;prior year periods, respectively. These decreases were primarily attributable to $699.2 million of non&#8209;cash impairments of goodwill and intangible assets and a $20.0 million other&#8209;than&#8209;temporary decrease in the fair value of the MedMen convertible note recorded in the prior year quarter, which did not repeat&#160;in the current period. In addition, the nine month period ended February 28, 2026, had lower&#160;amortization expense following the intangible asset impairment&#160;recorded during the fiscal quarter ended May 31, 2025, a $15.0 million gain related to the change in fair value of the Montauk contingent consideration, and&#160;lower selling and non&#8209;recurring litigation, and restructuring&#160;costs.&#160;These decreases were partially offset by higher general and administrative costs.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Office and general&#160;increased by&#160;34%&#160;and&#160;by&#160;3% during the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, when compared to the prior year period respectively. The increase in the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026 was primarily due to a $0.7 million increase in bad debt provisions within the distribution business, the inclusion of a full period of costs related to Craft Acquisition II, which was effective September 1, 2024 and contributed approximately $0.6 million to the period&#8209;over&#8209;period variance, and the absence of a $0.3 million property tax refund&#160;recorded in the prior year quarter.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company recognized stock-based compensation expense of&#160;$13.7&#160;million and&#160;$31.1 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to $4.0&#160;million and&#160;$18.2 million&#160;for the prior year period respectively. Stock-based compensation expense is primarily driven by time-based vesting schedules and may vary based on assumptions used in valuation and vesting models. The increase during the three and nine month periods was primarily due to the recognition of expense related to performance-based awards following the establishment and approval of their performance criteria during the second fiscal quarter. As a result, performance-based awards contributed approximately $6.3 million and $12.1 million of expense during the three and nine month periods, respectively. Stock based compensation expense in the prior year periods was lower primarily due to the cancellation of certain performance-based awards.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;">Insurance expense&#160;decreased by&#160;36%&#160;and&#160;by&#160;21% for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026 to $1.9&#160;million and&#160;$6.7 million&#160;from $2.9&#160;million and&#160;$8.6 million for&#160;the&#160;prior year period, respectively due to&#160;lower premiums as a result of management&#8217;s decision to self-insure a portion of our property and casualty insurance.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;">Rent expense&#160;increased by&#160;8%&#160;and&#160;decreased by&#160;6% for the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026&#160;to $0.8&#160;million and&#160;$2.9 million&#160;compared to&#160;$0.7&#160;million and&#160;$3.0 million for the&#160;prior year periods, respectively.&#160;Rent expense is predominantly comprised of&#160;operating lease expenses for our brew pubs and office spaces and varies period-over-period based on lease amortization schedules and common area maintenance&#160;costs.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Selling costs</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company incurred selling costs of&#160;$10.6&#160;million&#160;or&#160;5%&#160;of net revenue and&#160;$35.3 million or&#160;6%&#160;of net revenue as compared to&#160;$13.9&#160;million&#160;or&#160;7%&#160;of net revenue and&#160;$41.8 million or&#160;7%&#160;of net revenue in the prior year period respectively. These costs relate to third-party shipping costs for all segments, in addition to distributor commission incurred by the cannabis segment, Health Canada cannabis fees, and patient acquisition and maintenance costs. The&#160;decrease&#160;in selling costs for the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2026&#160;was primarily driven by lower freight costs in the beverage segment resulting from Project 420 cost&#8209;saving initiatives, which improved freight as a percentage of sales by approximately 90 and 144 basis points for the three and nine month periods, respectively. In addition, lower freight costs in the Canadian cannabis segment following contract renegotiations improved freight as a percentage of sales by approximately 180 and 210 basis points for the three and nine month periods, respectively, and were further supported by lower commission rates in the Canadian cannabis sales channels.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Amortization</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company incurred non-production related amortization charges of $5.1&#160;million and&#160;$13.4 million&#160;for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to&#160;$23.2&#160;million and&#160;$67.9 million&#160;in the prior year periods, respectively, based on depreciable capital and intangible assets useful lives. The&#160;decrease&#160;in the amortization expense is due to the lower carrying value of intangible assets as a result of the impairment charges recognized during the fiscal year&#160;ended&#160;May 31, 2025.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Marketing and promotion costs&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company incurred marketing and promotion costs of $8.7&#160;million and&#160;$28.8 million&#160;compared to&#160;$6.8&#160;million and&#160;$28.1 million for the prior year periods, respectively and was driven by variability in&#160;discretionary marketing spend.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Research and development</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Research and development costs were&#160;$0.1&#160;million and&#160;$0.2 million during the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to&#160;$0.1&#160;million and&#160;$0.3 million in the prior year periods, respectively. These costs relate to external expenditures&#160;associated with the development of new products.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Change in fair value of contingent consideration</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">A portion of the total consideration to be paid in connection with the Company&#8217;s acquisition&#160;of Montauk Brewing Company (&#8220;Montauk&#8221;) was&#160;contingent upon the achievement by Montauk of certain financial measures as of December 31, 2025. In the event that Montauk achieved either the pre-determined&#160;sales volume target or EBITDA target, then $15.0 million&#160;of contingent consideration would be deemed earned and payable. If both the sales volume target and the EBITDA target were achieved, an additional $3.0 million&#160;would be deemed earned and payable for a total contingent consideration payment of $18.0 million.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">For the year ended, May 31, 2025, the Company assessed the estimated value of the&#160;contingent consideration liability as $15.0 million, which was estimated to be achieved based on management&#8217;s forecast, applying a&#160;probability of achievement of&#160;100% for the&#160;sales volume target and&#160;0% on the remaining criteria, which was&#160;not&#160;expected to be achieved as EBITDA targets were not forecasted to be met.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the three months ended August 31, 2025, the Company reassessed the estimated fair value of the contingent consideration liability as $nil, based on subsequent information regarding Montauk&#8217;s operating results and revised expectations for the remainder of the earn&#8209;out period. As a result of lower&#8209;than&#8209;anticipated sales volumes during the peak selling periods of June, July and August 2025, and the&#160;loss of certain national retail programs, management concluded that Montauk no longer had a viable path to achieving the sales volume target or the&#160;EBITDA target&#160;within the earn&#8209;out period. Accordingly, the Company applied a probability of achievement of 0% to the&#160;sales volume target and 0% to the remaining criteria. The resulting $15.0 million&#160;change in fair value of the contingent consideration liability was recorded within the statement of profit and&#160;loss&#160;and&#160;contributed&#160;to the Company&#8217;s&#160;net income generated during the period ended August 31, 2025, despite historically reporting a net loss.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the three&#160;months ended February 28, 2026, the earn-out period concluded and neither financial measure was achieved. Accordingly, no further changes to&#160;the fair value of the contingent consideration liability were recognized during the three&#160;months ended February 28, 2026&#160;as no contingent consideration obligation was&#160;payable.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Impairments</b>&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the fiscal quarter ended February&#8239;28,&#8239;2026, the Company assessed for indicators of impairment and concluded that there were no indicators and accordingly,&#8239;no further impairment testing was required and no impairment charges were recognized during the period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the prior year period, based upon a combination of factors including a sustained decline in the Company&#8217;s market capitalization stemming from the uncertainty resulting from certain changes in U.S. global economic policy, including slower than anticipated progress in global cannabis legalization and overall declines in the craft beer industry sector,&#160;the Company concluded that it is more likely than&#160;not,&#160;that the fair value of our reporting units were&#160;less than their carrying amounts as of&#160;February 28, 2025.&#160;Accordingly, the Company utilized the income approach, which uses future discounted cash flows, to determine the fair value of each reporting unit. As a result, the Company&#160;recorded non-cash impairment charges of&#160;$570.0 million&#160;of cannabis goodwill, $100.0 million of beverage goodwill,&#160;$25.0 million of wellness goodwill and $4.2 million of distribution goodwill for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2025.&#160;The non-cash impairment charge had&#160;no&#160;impact on the Company&#8217;s compliance with debt covenants, its cash flows or available liquidity.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company&#8217;s cannabis goodwill assessment performed during&#160;the&#160;three&#160;and&#160;nine&#160;months ended&#160;February 28, 2025,&#160;the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;12.00%,&#160;a terminal growth rate of&#160;5%, and an average revenue growth rate of 34% over&#160;5&#160;years, based on an 88% and 40% average probability of&#160;anticipated EU and U.S. cannabis&#160;legalization, respectively and/or changes in drug policy in various countries within the next 5 years. A&#160;1%&#160;increase in the discount rate would result in an additional $285.0 million&#160;in impairment, a&#160;1%&#160;decrease in the terminal growth rate would result in an additional $210.0 million&#160;in impairment,&#160;a&#160;5%&#160;decrease in the average growth rate would result in an additional $170.0 million&#160;in impairment, a 5% decrease in the probability of EU cannabis legalization&#160;would result in an additional $80.0 million&#160;in impairment and a 5% decrease in the probability of US cannabis legalization&#160;would result in an additional $7.0 million&#160;in impairment.&#160;Changes to those probabilities resulting in continued delays in or cessation of legalization of cannabis within the United States and internationally, or adverse regulatory changes to existing legislation, could have an unfavorable impact on the estimated future cash flows, and ultimately, the fair value of the cannabis reporting unit, which may result in a material impairment expense recognized in future reporting periods.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company&#8217;s beverage goodwill assessment performed during&#160;the&#160;three&#160;and&#160;nine&#160;months ended&#160;February 28, 2025, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of 9.25%, a terminal growth rate of 2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of 12% over&#160;5&#160;years.&#160;A&#160;1%&#160;increase in the discount rate would result in an additional $70.0 million&#160;in impairment, a&#160;1%&#160;decrease in the terminal growth rate would result in an additional $50.0 million&#160;in impairment and a 1%&#160;decrease in the average growth rate would result in an additional $40.0&#160;million in impairment.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company&#8217;s wellness goodwill assessment performed during&#160;the&#160;three&#160;and&#160;nine&#160;months ended&#160;February 28, 2025, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;10.50%, a terminal growth rate of 2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of 7% over&#160;5&#160;years.&#160;A&#160;1%&#160;increase in the discount rate would result in an additional $5.0 million&#160;in impairment, a&#160;1%&#160;decrease in the terminal growth rate would result in an additional $3.0 million&#160;in impairment and a 1%&#160;decrease in the average growth rate would result in an additional $2.0 million&#160;in impairment.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company&#8217;s distribution&#160;goodwill assessment&#160;performed during&#160;the&#160;three&#160;and&#160;nine&#160;months ended&#160;February 28, 2025, the Company recorded $4.2 million of impairments which brought the remaining distribution goodwill balance to $nil.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Other than temporary write-down of convertible notes receivable</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company no longer held&#160;MedMen Convertible Notes, and thus did not recognize any further changes in fair value.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">During the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2025, the Company recognized an&#160;other-than-temporary change in fair value, which resulted in a non-cash expense&#160;of $20.0 million and $20.0 million. The&#160;MedMen Convertible Note was valued based upon the estimated fair value of the&#160;collateral assets net of estimated disposal costs and has been reduced to reflect recent developments in restructuring efforts.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Subsequent to the impairment recorded during the&#160;three and nine months ended February 28, 2025,&#160;MedMen exited receivership and substantially all of its remaining assets were transferred to a new entity owned by MedMen&#8217;s secured creditors, including SH Acquisition. In connection with the foregoing, the Company disposed&#160;of its MedMen Convertible Note in exchange for on option to acquire a&#160;68% membership interest in&#160;SH Acquisition&#160;for $1.00&#160;upon U.S. federal cannabis legalization. See Note 8&#160;(Long-term investments). This option was recorded as a Level&#160;3&#160;equity investment measured at fair value by assessing the discounted cash flows of&#160;SH Acquisition.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Litigation costs, net of recoveries&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company recorded&#160;$0.6&#160;million and&#160;$2.5 million&#160;of litigation settlements costs and third-party fees incurred in defending these claims, net of favorable recoveries compared to&#160;$2.8&#160;million and&#160;$5.3 million in the prior year period respectively. The&#160;decrease is related to period-to-period variability as litigation and settlement costs&#160;are&#160;non-recurring in nature.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Restructuring costs </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">In connection with the integration of certain acquisitions and strategic transactions, the Company has incurred restructuring and exit costs in the amount of&#160;$4.1&#160;million and&#160;$5.9 million for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, compared to $6.1&#160;million and&#160;$17.2 million&#160;for the prior year period respectively. All restructuring&#160;plans are approved at the executive level, and their associated expenses are recognized in&#160;the period in which the plan is&#160;committed or otherwise incurred.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Within the Cannabis segment,&#160;during&#160;the nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company incurred restructuring&#160;expenses totaling $5.2&#160;million. These charges included $3.7 million&#160;associated with the restructuring of the Quebec facility to transition from vegetable cultivation to cannabis cultivation in response to increased&#160;global cannabis demand,&#160;$1.0 million&#160;related to&#160;employee termination severance and benefits associated with the reorganization of the Canadian cannabis commercial function, and $0.2 million related to the wind-down of certain non-operating entities.&#160;Additionally, the Company recognized $0.3&#160;million related to its Fort Collins, CO partially vacant warehouse that was previously&#160;held for&#160;sale and was divested during the three&#160;months ended February 28, 2026. See Note 3 (capital assets).&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">During the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company accrued $8.5 million of restructuring&#160;charges related to the closure of Hop Valley and other Project 420&#160;initiatives within the Beverage segment, of which $7.5 million was recognized in&#160;nine months ended February 28, 2026, thereby&#160;reducing the accrual to $1.0 million.&#160;In addition, during the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, the Company incurred $0.7 million&#160;of restructuring related expenses associated with the Atwater Brewery, primarily related to the asset being classified as held for sale and additional facility restructuring activities. See Note 3 (Capital Assets).&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Transaction (income) costs, net</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Transaction (income) costs, net, include&#160;non-recurring acquisition related income and expenses, related legal, financial advisor and due diligence cost and expenses and transaction related compensation.&#160;For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, transaction (income) costs&#160;increased to&#160;$1.9&#160;million and&#160;$2.9&#160;million&#160;from&#160;$0.6&#160;million and&#160;$2.6 million for the prior year periods, respectively.&#160;During the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, transaction costs were primarily attributable to $1.2 million of legacy HEXO pre-acquisition tax settlements and $0.6 million of due diligence costs associated with ongoing transactions. In comparison, transaction costs during the prior year nine month period were primarily comprised of $1.1 million of costs related to the completion of&#160;Craft Acquisition II.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-operating (expense) income, net</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">During the three and nine months ended February 28, 2026&#160;and February 28, 2025, respectively, the changes in non-operating (expense), income were comprised of:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-indent: 0px;">

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures to GAAP Measures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted EBITDA</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure that does not have any standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The Company calculates adjusted EBITDA as net loss/net income before income taxes, net interest expense, depreciation and amortization, purchase price accounting step-up on inventory,&#160;stock-based compensation,&#160;impairments, other than temporary change in fair value of convertible notes receivable,&#160;restructuring costs, transaction (income) costs net, litigation costs net of recoveries, change in fair value of contingent consideration, project 420 cost savings initiatives, unrealized currency gains and losses and other adjustments.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">We believe&#160;that this presentation provides useful information to management, analysts and investors regarding certain additional financial and business trends relating to the Company&#8217;s results of operations and financial condition. In addition, management uses this measure for reviewing the financial results of the Company and as a component of performance-based executive compensation.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">We do not consider adjusted EBITDA in isolation or as an alternative to financial measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The principal limitation of adjusted EBITDA is that it excludes certain expenses and income that are required by U.S. GAAP to be recorded in our consolidated financial statements. In addition, adjusted EBITDA is subject to inherent limitations as this metric reflects the exercise of judgment by management about which expenses and income are excluded or included in determining adjusted EBITDA. In order to compensate for these limitations, management presents adjusted EBITDA in connection with GAAP results.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">For three and nine months ended February 28, 2026, adjusted EBITDA&#160;increased to&#160;$10.7&#160;million and&#160;increased&#160;to&#160;$29.3&#160;million compared to $9.0&#160;million and $27.4&#160;million for&#160;the prior year periods and remained improved&#160;as we continue to execute on our strategic plan.</p>
